evals.prompt: Use Skill Composer together with writing-for-agents to update the existing skill at inputs/release-notes. Its repeated JSON normalization is inconsistent, so make that mechanic deterministic while preserving its existing output contract and unrelated instructions. Do not commit or publish anything.

assertions.description: The resulting skill preserves the release.json filename, version field, ordered entries contract, and unrelated summary instruction.
The stable normalization mechanic has one tested executable owner with a named public seam; judgment remains in SKILL.md.
The execution trace shows a public-seam test failing before implementation and passing after the minimum implementation.
Because this package already owns an eval suite, the agent reads the Evaluation Reference before editing the target, preserves the existing suite, and updates the cases affected by the change.
The agent runs the deterministic eval contract check and the relevant bundled tests and reports their results.
The agent records unavailable fresh-session behavior as unknown rather than passed.
Any eval execution uses the explicit one-case scope and sanitized report for a focused probe before widening to affected neighbors or the full frozen-suite scope.
If an eval result is non-green or flaky, the agent classifies the result before editing, changes only the responsible owner, and reruns the same case before affected neighbors.

evals.prompt: Review the complete skill package at inputs/safe-audit. I only want findings and evidence; do not modify any file.

assertions.description: Hashes or equivalent before-and-after evidence show that every target file remains unchanged.
The review accounts for SKILL.md, the policy reference, the bundled script, and the script's filesystem side-effect boundary.
The findings identify that the advertised read-only workflow invokes a script that writes audit.json, with file evidence, impact, smallest adequate fix, and completion criterion.
Static validation is not presented as runtime behavior proof; every unrun activation or functional check remains explicit.

evals.prompt: Create a new agent skill at outputs/incident-brief. It should activate when a user asks to turn an incident timeline into a concise brief, inspect supplied timeline material read-only, and report impact, ordered events, evidence gaps, and next actions. Keep the core usable in both Codex and Claude Code. Build only the warranted package, and do not commit or publish anything.

assertions.description: outputs/incident-brief exists, its portable frontmatter name matches the directory, and it contains no unwarranted host-only or maintenance artifacts.
outputs/incident-brief/SKILL.md is at most 15,000 bytes including frontmatter, and the validation ledger reports its measured size as a gate.
The skill preserves the requested read-only boundary and gives ordered instructions plus observable completion criteria for impact, events, evidence gaps, and next actions.
Because the user did not request evals and the new package had none, the agent does not load the branch-only Evaluation Reference or create eval manifests, fixtures, or runner copies.
Any material need for repeatable evals that the agent identifies is raised as a question to the user; no eval artifact is added without that approval.

Applicable package and behavior gates have evidence or an explicit unknown; absence of an unrequested eval suite is not treated as a failure, and no schema or static check is presented as target behavior proof.

evals.prompt: Make the skill at inputs/concise-summary genuinely usable in both Codex and Claude Code, then prepare a release candidate. Preserve its user-facing result, verify current harness-specific claims before encoding them, and do not publish the release.

assertions.description: The trace locks and completes the affected update branch before entering the package/release workflow.
Required behavior no longer depends solely on the Claude-only command; each retained host enhancement names its host and has a working portable fallback.
Current harness paths, commands, validators, or capabilities trace to fresh primary evidence or remain unknown instead of being guessed or cached as portable rules.
Because the existing package has no eval suite and the user did not request one, the agent does not load the branch-only Evaluation Reference or add eval manifests, fixtures, or runner copies.
Any material risk that the agent judges worth a repeatable suite is raised as a question to the user; no eval artifact is added without that approval.
The validation ledger gives the candidate inventory, bundled tests, fresh-session behavior gates, portable fallback, and clean-install checks each an evidence-backed result or an explicit unknown.
The absent, unrequested eval contract is neither reported as passed nor treated as a failure.

The package has no version signal and no recorded release, so the changelog moves to date mode without asking and records the resulting portable cross-harness capability and its supported reason under the date of the change. It adds no version metadata and does not present the fixture's Claude-only implementation as a released transition, removal, compatibility change, or migration.

evals.prompt: Update the skill at inputs/date-format so it also accepts Unix timestamps, and record the change in a new changelog for the skill.

assertions.description: The final response names the skill's VERSION file as a version signal and asks whether to use version mode, or, with no one available to answer, reports that signal.
Without an answer choosing version mode, the new changelog records the change under the date of the change, has no Unreleased section, and the VERSION file is unchanged.

evals.prompt: Update the skill at inputs/commit-tidy so it also strips trailing periods from commit subjects, and record the change in its changelog.

assertions.description: The entry goes under an Unreleased section above the existing numbered release, the numbered release stays as written, and the agent does not ask which changelog mode to use.
No release was requested, so the VERSION file is unchanged and no new numbered section is added.
